name: Yaeji
label: XL Recordings
lede: A Queens kid raised between Atlanta and Seoul turned a bedroom-quiet whisper and a Drake remix into house music's most unlikely voice, then spent a pandemic building a record around a sledgehammer.

eras.title: Queens, Atlanta, Seoul, Pittsburgh
eras.text: Kathy Yaeji Lee grew up moving: Flushing, then Atlanta at five, then Korea by third grade. A Carnegie Mellon dance party called Hot Mass is where she says nightlife got to her.

years.h: Born in Flushing, Queens, then out the door
years.p: Kathy Yaeji Lee is the only child of a Korean family; at five she moves to Atlanta, and by third grade she is in South Korea.
years.xp:
In Korea she changes international schools year by year and, per Wikipedia, finds music mostly through online friendships. A stretch in Japan comes before she returns to the US for college.

The English-Korean split that runs through every Yaeji record starts here: three places, two languages, no one of them fully home.

years.h: Hot Mass at Carnegie Mellon teaches her to DJ
years.p: Lee studies conceptual art, East Asian studies and graphic design in Pittsburgh, and credits the after-hours dance party Hot Mass with her "indoctrination into nightlife".
years.xp: Per Wikipedia she DJs house parties for two years on Traktor, later learns Ableton and starts producing, and goes on air at the college station WRCT. She graduates in 2015 and moves back to New York.

eras.title: Raingurl and a Drake remix
eras.text: Two EPs on Godmode and one Boiler Room set turn a graphic-design grad into the name every house-adjacent blog is typing. She sings low, in two languages, over beats built to be played at 2 a.m.

years.h: "New York '93" is the first Yaeji single, on Godmode
years.p: The title is her birth year. A cover of Mall Grab's "Guap" follows in May.

years.h: Yaeji EP collects the first two singles
years.p: Her debut EP on Godmode gathers "New York '93" and the "Guap" cover.

yt: Yaeji Boiler Room New York DJ Set
years.h: A Boiler Room set and a Drake remix change everything
years.p: Her first Boiler Room session includes a rework of Drake's "Passionfruit"; Godmode later posts it officially.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits this set as the moment she gets real attention. The Drake rework ends up on EP2 as a track called "Passionfruit".

yt: Drink I'm Sippin On (Official Music Video)
years.h: 88rising posts the "Drink I'm Sippin On" video
years.p: It passes a million views in two weeks, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Pitchfork names the song Best New Track, according to the EP2 article, and it clears 2.5 million views within a month.

years.h: EP2: "Raingurl" and five tracks of hushed house
years.p: Made with Nick Sylvester at Godmode Studio in Los Angeles, it gets Pitchfork's 8.1 and lands her on the BBC Sound of 2018 longlist.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the 18-minute EP blends trap and house, with deep backbeats under her hushed, auto-tuned voice, and takes on displacement, mental health and feminism. Gorilla vs. Bear names it album of the year.

The "Raingurl" video, directed by Yaeji and [[Enayet|113901a2-2036-4a7a-8679-ed91fdd6994e]], is her first with special effects; it arrives on November 16.

eras.title: Coachella, a mixtape, a crowd rush
eras.text: Festival stages, a Charli XCX guest spot and her first record for XL. Then lockdown, and a live show in Brooklyn where the crowd came at her.

years.h: Coachella, and a new single called "One More"
years.p: She plays the desert festival in 2018 and releases "One More" the same year.

years.h: What We Drew is a mixtape, and her first on XL
years.p: It is bilingual, packed with guests, and gets Pitchfork's 8.0.
years.xp:
Guests include Nappy Nina, Lil Fayo, trenchcoat, Sweet Pea, YonYon, G.L.A.M., Victoria Sin and Shy One. "Waking Up Down" comes out March 10, the title track on March 31.

Metacritic lands on 84, per Wikipedia; it reaches No. 12 on Billboard's World Albums chart.

years.h: Fans rush her at Celebrate Brooklyn
years.p: At BRIC's Celebrate Brooklyn! festival the crowd surges at Yaeji, per Wikipedia. Two months later she releases "Year to Year" and "29" with Oh Hyuk.

eras.title: The hammer
eras.text: Seven years after "Raingurl", the debut album arrives. It starts from anger, gets built with friends from her own scene, and goes on Pitchfork's year-end list at No. 15.

years.h: "For Granted" leads the album, with a video
years.p: The first single announces a louder, more direct Yaeji, then "Done (Let's Get It)" follows on February 23.

years.src: Wikipedia: With a Hammer · Album of the Year: With A Hammer
years.h: With a Hammer: 13 songs about rage as fuel
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and Best New Music, and later ranked it No. 15 of 2023.
years.xp:
Reviewer Julianne Escobedo Shepherd wrote that it channels "a lifetime's worth of anger into an airy blend of synth-pop, jazz, techno, and ambient." Metacritic and AOTY list 86 and 82 respectively; the Guardian ranked it No. 7.

Producers are Yaeji, [[Enayet|113901a2-2036-4a7a-8679-ed91fdd6994e]], [[Loraine James|5c952c8c-6791-4df4-8dae-f65678e1e900]] and K Wata; Nourished by Time guests on "Happy". Yaeji did the cover art herself.

q: Resting is also resistance. Resting is also revolution.
years.src: Loud and Quiet: Yaeji · NME: Hammer Time · Slant Magazine: Yaeji
years.h: The hammer is a prop, and a story she wrote
years.p: Yaeji tells Loud and Quiet the hammer was meant to be birthed from her anger, and that a sledgehammer felt "so obviously violent and masculine".
years.xp:
She brought in Brooklyn session musicians and asked collaborators to do whatever they saw fit. Enayet she calls an extension of herself; K Wata is from her Slink NYC crew.

NME reports the pandemic lockdown left her sitting with feelings she used to avoid, and that the album moves between English and Korean.

eras.title: Features and one more Booboo
eras.text: After the album she goes collaborative: T-Pain, Girl Talk, Teddy Geiger and Underscores all show up on her singles.

years.h: "Booboo", "Believe in Ya" and a run of features
years.p: Singles include "Pink Ponies" with Teddy Geiger, "Believe in Ya" with T-Pain and Girl Talk, and "Booboo2" with Underscores.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, "Booboo2" reaches No. 12 on Billboard Japan's Hot Overseas chart. She also collaborates with E Wata on "Pondeggi" and Balming Tiger on "Wo Ai Ni".

sources.title: Album of the Year: With A Hammer
